Model 1:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$ | disruption time window on blocked segment $s^* \in S$ (partial blockage: only one track usable) |
| $P_i \subseteq S$ | ordered sequence of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,s}^{k}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}^{k}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, segment separation (same direction) |
| $h^{bi}$ | minimum headway between opposing trains on the shared (opposite-direction) track during disruption |
| $d_i^{sch}, a_i^{sch}$ | scheduled departure/arrival times at origin/destination |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation in the objective |
| $C_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $H^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround/dwell time at stations |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t^{res}$ | time at which the disrupted track is restored |

## 3. Variables

**Rescheduling:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at the boundary of segment $s$ (station node).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$.
- $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ run in **opposite directions** and $i$ uses the shared track before $j$.
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies the shared opposite track on segment $s$ during the disruption (rerouting).

**Speed selection:**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \big[(a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}) + (d_{i,1} - d_i^{sch})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in P_i}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

(Delay terms can be linearized with $\ge 0$ auxiliary variables $D_i \ge a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}$, $D_i \ge 0$.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_i} \delta_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (retiming via speed choice):**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s'} = \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k} \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i,\; s' = \text{downstream node of } s$$

**(C3) Minimum dwell/turnaround at stations:**
$$a_{i,s} + H^{turn} \le d_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; \forall \text{ station nodes } s$$

**(C4) Cancellation forbids movement:**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i), \qquad a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, allows reordering):**
$$a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{seg} - M(1 - x_{ij}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$
$$a_{i,s} - a_{j,s} \ge h^{seg} - M\,x_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$

**(C6) Station headways (arrival/departure):**
$$d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1-x_{ij}), \qquad a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{arr} - M(1-x_{ij})$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M x_{ij}$, for all $(i,j)\in O$, stations $s$.

**(C7) Rerouting to the shared opposite track during disruption:**
$$u_{i,s^*} \le y^{win}_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i$$
where $y^{win}_{i,s^*}$ (linearized) enforces that train $i$ may use the shared track only if its occupancy window intersects $\mathcal{D}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \le t_d^{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s^*}), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s^*})$$
i.e., $u_{i,s^*}=1$ only if the train is on $s^*$ within the disruption window; otherwise it must wait for $t^{res}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^{res} - M\,u_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i \text{ (single-track direction)}$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track:** for opposing trains $i,j$ both potentially on $s^*$ during $\mathcal{D}$:
$$d_{i,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
so if both use the shared track, exactly one order ($z_{ij}$ or $1-z_{ij}$) is enforced.

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-cycle / transitivity on triplets):**
$$x_{ij} + x_{jk} - x_{ik} \le 1, \quad x_{ij} + x_{jk} \ge x_{ik} \quad \forall i,j,k \in T$$

**(C10) Time bounds:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling variables** ($a, d, x, y$) allow retiming (C2 with chosen running times), reordering (C5–C6, C9), and cancellation (C4, C10).
- **Rerouting** is captured by $u_{i,s^*}$: during the disruption window trains may be routed onto the opposite track (C7); otherwise they must wait until restoration.
- **Speed management** is modeled by discrete profiles $\delta_{i,s}^k$ with fixed $(r^k, e^k)$ pairs, coupling timetable decisions and energy (C1–C2). Slower profiles reduce energy but may increase delays — the objective trades these off.
- **Safety** is ensured by headway constraints on segments and stations (C5–C6) and by the big-M bidirectional conflict constraints (C8) preventing simultaneous opposing occupancy of the shared track.
- **Objective** minimizes weighted total delay, total traction energy, and cancellation penalties, with weights $\alpha, \beta$ tuning the trade-off.

All constraints are linear; binary variables are $y_i, x_{ij}, z_{ij}, u_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}^k$, so the model is a valid MILP.

Model 2:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $P$ | set of platform tracks at each station, indexed $p$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^-, t_d^+]$ | disruption time window during which one track of a blocked segment $s^* \in S$ is unavailable |
| $U$ | set of trains eligible for cancellation, indexed $u$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $h^{seg}, h^{arr}, h^{dep}$ | minimum headways: same-direction segment, arrival, departure |
| $\tau_i^{run}(s,k)$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_i(s,k)$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $\tau_i^{dwell}(s)$ | planned dwell time of train $i$ at station bounding segment $s$ |
| $t_i^{sched}(s)$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority) |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation penalty |
| $C_u$ | cancellation penalty of train $u$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $\bar{t}$ | planning horizon end |
| $o_i \in \{0,1\}$ | parameter: 1 if train $i$ is scheduled on the track opposite to the blocked one (direction indicator) |

## 3. Variables

**Timing variables**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ from the start of segment $s$
- $\delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0$: arrival / departure delay

**Speed profile selection**
- $x_{isk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$

**Routing / reordering / rerouting**
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ (ordering variable, $i<j$)
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite (shared) track on segment $s$ during the disruption
- $q_{isp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies platform track $p$ at station $s$

**Cancellation**
- $c_u \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $u$ is cancelled

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \big(w_i \delta_{is}^{arr} + w_i \delta_{is}^{dep}\big)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_i(s,k)\, x_{isk}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{u \in U} C_u c_u}_{\text{cancellation penalties}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{is}^{arr} \ge a_{is} - t_i^{sched}(s), \quad \delta_{is}^{arr} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (speed profile coupling)**
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} \tau_i^{run}(s,k)\, x_{isk} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Dwell time**
$$
d_{i,s+1} \ge a_{is} + \tau_i^{dwell}(s+1) \qquad \forall i,\; s = 1,\dots,|S|-1
$$

**(C4) Speed profile uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in U,\; \forall s; \qquad \sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \setminus U,\; \forall s
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segments (with reordering)**
For all pairs $i < j$ on the same track and direction:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{seg} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M c_j
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js} + h^{seg} - M\, y_{ij} - M c_i
$$

**(C6) Rerouting to the opposite track during disruption**
For segment $s^*$ and $t \in \mathcal{D}$: a train may use the blocked track only if it does not traverse during $\mathcal{D}$, or it is rerouted:
$$
a_{is^*} \ge t_d^+ - M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) - M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \le t_d^- + M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) + M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
i.e., if $z_{is^*}=0$ and the train is not cancelled, it must completely avoid $\mathcal{D}$ on the blocked track; $z_{is^*}=1$ forces rerouting to the shared opposite track.

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track**
Trains rerouted onto the shared track ($z=1$) and trains normally operating in the opposite direction ($o_j = 1$) must not occupy segment $s^*$ simultaneously. For all pairs $i,j$ with $o_j = 1$:
$$
d_{js^*} \ge a_{is^*} + h^{seg} - M(3 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) - y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \ge a_{js^*} + h^{seg} - M(2 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) + y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
The big-M structure ensures these constraints are active only when train $i$ is rerouted onto the shared track and train $j$ runs in the opposite direction, with the ordering variable $y_{ij}$ selecting which train goes first.

**(C8) Station headways (arrival/departure)**
For trains assigned to the same platform track $p$ at station $s$:
$$
a_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{arr} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
$$
d_{js} \ge d_{is} + h^{dep} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M y_{ij}$.

**(C9) Platform track assignment uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} q_{isp} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s \text{ (station nodes)}
$$

**(C10) Horizon bounds**
$$
a_{is} \le \bar{t}, \quad d_{is} \le \bar{t} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C11) Variable domains**
$$
x_{isk}, y_{ij}, z_{is}, q_{isp}, c_u \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Model Explanation

- **Rescheduling:** Constraints (C1)–(C3) allow retiming (shifted arrival/departure) and enforce physical running and dwell times; reordering is enabled by the binary $y_{ij}$ in (C5), (C7), (C8).
- **Speed management:** Each train–segment picks exactly one discrete profile (C4); each profile has a fixed running time and energy, coupling the timing and energy dimensions of the objective.
- **Disruption handling:** (C6) forces trains either to wait until the disruption ends or to be rerouted to the opposite track; (C7) guarantees conflict-free bidirectional operation on the shared track.
- **Cancellations:** $c_u$ deactivates all constraints of a cancelled train via big-M terms and adds penalty $\beta C_u$.
- **Objective:** trades off weighted delays, energy (favoring slower profiles), and cancellation costs.

The model is linear: all nonlinearities are avoided through the big-M disjunctive formulation and binary ordering variables.

Model 3:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $D \subset T \times T$ | ordered pairs of trains that may conflict (same direction) |
| $O \subset T \times T$ | pairs of trains running in **opposite directions** (bidirectional conflicts on shared track) |
| $\mathcal{B} \subset S$ | set of blocked segments during disruption window $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ |
| $P$ | set of cancellation decisions, $P \subseteq T$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r^{k}_{is}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $e^{k}_{is}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival, departure at stations, and segment separation |
| $d^{sch}_{is}, a^{sch}_{is}$ | scheduled departure/arrival of train $i$ at boundary of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority class) |
| $\alpha$ | monetary cost per unit of energy |
| $\beta_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $x^{ref}_{is}$ | =1 if rerouting to the opposite track is allowed for train $i$ on segment $s$ (only during $[t^{dis}_1,t^{dis}_2]$ and on blocked segments) |
| $H^{opp}$ | headway for opposite-direction trains sharing the same physical track |

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at the start of segment $s$

**Binary:**
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $s$
- $u_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ (written $u_{is,k}$)
- $\delta_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variable, =1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $\sigma_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ passes train $j$ (reordering) before segment $s$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \sum_{s \in S} \big[(a_{is} - a^{sch}_{is}) + (d_{is} - d^{sch}_{is})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k}}_{\text{energy cost}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} \beta_i y_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
\tag{1}
$$

(Delays can be linearized with $D_{is} \ge a_{is}-a^{sch}_{is}$, $D_{is}\ge 0$ if only positive delays are penalized.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness — exactly one profile per train-segment:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} u_{is,k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency (retiming via profile choice):**
$$
d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} r^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k} \le a_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{3}
$$

**(C3) Train chain continuity (no overtaking within a train's own path):**
$$
a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{4}
$$

**(C4) Dwell time at stations:**
$$
a_{i,s} + \tau^{min}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i,\ s \text{ at station boundaries} \tag{5}
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, with reordering):**
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge h^{seg} - M(1-\delta_{ij,s}) - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge h^{seg} - M\,\delta_{ij,s} - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6b}
$$

Analogous pairs with $d_{is}$ using $h^{dep}$ and with $a_{is}$ vs $d_{js}$ using $h^{arr}$.

**(C6) Rerouting to opposite track (only during disruption, only on blocked segments):**
$$
z_{is} \le x^{ref}_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{7}
$$
$$
z_{is} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ s \notin \mathcal{B} \tag{8}
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track:** if train $i$ (direction A) is rerouted onto the opposite track, it must not conflict with train $j$ (direction B) using its own track:
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - \delta_{ij,s}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - (1-\delta_{ij,s})) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9b}
$$

**(C8) Blocked segment closure during disruption window:** trains may traverse blocked segment $s \in \mathcal{B}$ only if rerouted ($z_{is}=1$) or outside the window:
$$
a_{is} \le t^{dis}_1 + M(1 - \lambda_{is}) \quad\text{or}\quad a_{is} \ge t^{dis}_2 - M \lambda_{is},\quad \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\lambda_{is} \le z_{is} + (1 - \text{window overlap indicator}) \quad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{10}
$$

**(C9) Reordering (overtaking) consistency across consecutive segments:**
$$
\delta_{ij,s} - \delta_{ij,s+1} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j, \qquad
\delta_{ij,s+1} - \delta_{ij,s} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j \tag{11}
$$
(overtaking allowed only if the passing variable $\sigma$ is activated, which in practice requires station tracks).

**(C10) Cancellation propagation:** a cancelled train occupies no resources:
$$
d_{is},\ a_{is} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i,\ s \tag{12}
$$

**(C11) Schedule adherence bounds / recovery limits:**
$$
a_{is} \le a^{sch}_{is} + \Delta^{max}_i \quad \forall i, s \tag{13}
$$

**(C12) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0; \quad y_i, z_{is}, u_{is,k}, \delta_{ij,s}, \sigma_{ij,s}, \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\} \tag{14}
$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling:** continuous $a_{is}, d_{is}$ allow retiming; binaries $\delta_{ij,s}$ allow resequencing (6), and $\sigma_{ij,s}$ permits overtaking at stations (11).
- **Rerouting:** $z_{is}$ sends a train onto the opposite track during the partial blockage (7)–(8); constraints (9) prevent head-on conflicts on the shared physical track.
- **Speed management:** discrete profiles $u_{is,k}$ couple running time (3) and energy (objective) — slower profiles save energy but may increase delays, capturing the delay–energy trade-off.
- **Cancellation:** $y_i$ removes a train entirely at penalty $\beta_i$ (2, 12).
- **Disruption handling:** (10) forbids occupancy of blocked segments during $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ unless rerouted.
- **Objective (1)** balances weighted delays, energy cost, and cancellation penalties, yielding a linear MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut.

response.content:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$ | disruption time window on blocked segment $s^* \in S$ (partial blockage: only one track usable) |
| $P_i \subseteq S$ | ordered sequence of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,s}^{k}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}^{k}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, segment separation (same direction) |
| $h^{bi}$ | minimum headway between opposing trains on the shared (opposite-direction) track during disruption |
| $d_i^{sch}, a_i^{sch}$ | scheduled departure/arrival times at origin/destination |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation in the objective |
| $C_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $H^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround/dwell time at stations |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t^{res}$ | time at which the disrupted track is restored |

## 3. Variables

**Rescheduling:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at the boundary of segment $s$ (station node).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$.
- $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ run in **opposite directions** and $i$ uses the shared track before $j$.
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies the shared opposite track on segment $s$ during the disruption (rerouting).

**Speed selection:**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \big[(a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}) + (d_{i,1} - d_i^{sch})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in P_i}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

(Delay terms can be linearized with $\ge 0$ auxiliary variables $D_i \ge a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}$, $D_i \ge 0$.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_i} \delta_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (retiming via speed choice):**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s'} = \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k} \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i,\; s' = \text{downstream node of } s$$

**(C3) Minimum dwell/turnaround at stations:**
$$a_{i,s} + H^{turn} \le d_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; \forall \text{ station nodes } s$$

**(C4) Cancellation forbids movement:**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i), \qquad a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, allows reordering):**
$$a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{seg} - M(1 - x_{ij}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$
$$a_{i,s} - a_{j,s} \ge h^{seg} - M\,x_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$

**(C6) Station headways (arrival/departure):**
$$d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1-x_{ij}), \qquad a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{arr} - M(1-x_{ij})$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M x_{ij}$, for all $(i,j)\in O$, stations $s$.

**(C7) Rerouting to the shared opposite track during disruption:**
$$u_{i,s^*} \le y^{win}_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i$$
where $y^{win}_{i,s^*}$ (linearized) enforces that train $i$ may use the shared track only if its occupancy window intersects $\mathcal{D}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \le t_d^{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s^*}), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s^*})$$
i.e., $u_{i,s^*}=1$ only if the train is on $s^*$ within the disruption window; otherwise it must wait for $t^{res}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^{res} - M\,u_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i \text{ (single-track direction)}$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track:** for opposing trains $i,j$ both potentially on $s^*$ during $\mathcal{D}$:
$$d_{i,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
so if both use the shared track, exactly one order ($z_{ij}$ or $1-z_{ij}$) is enforced.

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-cycle / transitivity on triplets):**
$$x_{ij} + x_{jk} - x_{ik} \le 1, \quad x_{ij} + x_{jk} \ge x_{ik} \quad \forall i,j,k \in T$$

**(C10) Time bounds:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling variables** ($a, d, x, y$) allow retiming (C2 with chosen running times), reordering (C5–C6, C9), and cancellation (C4, C10).
- **Rerouting** is captured by $u_{i,s^*}$: during the disruption window trains may be routed onto the opposite track (C7); otherwise they must wait until restoration.
- **Speed management** is modeled by discrete profiles $\delta_{i,s}^k$ with fixed $(r^k, e^k)$ pairs, coupling timetable decisions and energy (C1–C2). Slower profiles reduce energy but may increase delays — the objective trades these off.
- **Safety** is ensured by headway constraints on segments and stations (C5–C6) and by the big-M bidirectional conflict constraints (C8) preventing simultaneous opposing occupancy of the shared track.
- **Objective** minimizes weighted total delay, total traction energy, and cancellation penalties, with weights $\alpha, \beta$ tuning the trade-off.

All constraints are linear; binary variables are $y_i, x_{ij}, z_{ij}, u_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}^k$, so the model is a valid MILP.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $P$ | set of platform tracks at each station, indexed $p$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^-, t_d^+]$ | disruption time window during which one track of a blocked segment $s^* \in S$ is unavailable |
| $U$ | set of trains eligible for cancellation, indexed $u$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $h^{seg}, h^{arr}, h^{dep}$ | minimum headways: same-direction segment, arrival, departure |
| $\tau_i^{run}(s,k)$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_i(s,k)$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $\tau_i^{dwell}(s)$ | planned dwell time of train $i$ at station bounding segment $s$ |
| $t_i^{sched}(s)$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority) |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation penalty |
| $C_u$ | cancellation penalty of train $u$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $\bar{t}$ | planning horizon end |
| $o_i \in \{0,1\}$ | parameter: 1 if train $i$ is scheduled on the track opposite to the blocked one (direction indicator) |

## 3. Variables

**Timing variables**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ from the start of segment $s$
- $\delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0$: arrival / departure delay

**Speed profile selection**
- $x_{isk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$

**Routing / reordering / rerouting**
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ (ordering variable, $i<j$)
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite (shared) track on segment $s$ during the disruption
- $q_{isp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies platform track $p$ at station $s$

**Cancellation**
- $c_u \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $u$ is cancelled

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \big(w_i \delta_{is}^{arr} + w_i \delta_{is}^{dep}\big)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_i(s,k)\, x_{isk}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{u \in U} C_u c_u}_{\text{cancellation penalties}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{is}^{arr} \ge a_{is} - t_i^{sched}(s), \quad \delta_{is}^{arr} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (speed profile coupling)**
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} \tau_i^{run}(s,k)\, x_{isk} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Dwell time**
$$
d_{i,s+1} \ge a_{is} + \tau_i^{dwell}(s+1) \qquad \forall i,\; s = 1,\dots,|S|-1
$$

**(C4) Speed profile uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in U,\; \forall s; \qquad \sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \setminus U,\; \forall s
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segments (with reordering)**
For all pairs $i < j$ on the same track and direction:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{seg} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M c_j
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js} + h^{seg} - M\, y_{ij} - M c_i
$$

**(C6) Rerouting to the opposite track during disruption**
For segment $s^*$ and $t \in \mathcal{D}$: a train may use the blocked track only if it does not traverse during $\mathcal{D}$, or it is rerouted:
$$
a_{is^*} \ge t_d^+ - M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) - M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \le t_d^- + M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) + M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
i.e., if $z_{is^*}=0$ and the train is not cancelled, it must completely avoid $\mathcal{D}$ on the blocked track; $z_{is^*}=1$ forces rerouting to the shared opposite track.

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track**
Trains rerouted onto the shared track ($z=1$) and trains normally operating in the opposite direction ($o_j = 1$) must not occupy segment $s^*$ simultaneously. For all pairs $i,j$ with $o_j = 1$:
$$
d_{js^*} \ge a_{is^*} + h^{seg} - M(3 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) - y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \ge a_{js^*} + h^{seg} - M(2 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) + y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
The big-M structure ensures these constraints are active only when train $i$ is rerouted onto the shared track and train $j$ runs in the opposite direction, with the ordering variable $y_{ij}$ selecting which train goes first.

**(C8) Station headways (arrival/departure)**
For trains assigned to the same platform track $p$ at station $s$:
$$
a_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{arr} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
$$
d_{js} \ge d_{is} + h^{dep} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M y_{ij}$.

**(C9) Platform track assignment uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} q_{isp} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s \text{ (station nodes)}
$$

**(C10) Horizon bounds**
$$
a_{is} \le \bar{t}, \quad d_{is} \le \bar{t} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C11) Variable domains**
$$
x_{isk}, y_{ij}, z_{is}, q_{isp}, c_u \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Model Explanation

- **Rescheduling:** Constraints (C1)–(C3) allow retiming (shifted arrival/departure) and enforce physical running and dwell times; reordering is enabled by the binary $y_{ij}$ in (C5), (C7), (C8).
- **Speed management:** Each train–segment picks exactly one discrete profile (C4); each profile has a fixed running time and energy, coupling the timing and energy dimensions of the objective.
- **Disruption handling:** (C6) forces trains either to wait until the disruption ends or to be rerouted to the opposite track; (C7) guarantees conflict-free bidirectional operation on the shared track.
- **Cancellations:** $c_u$ deactivates all constraints of a cancelled train via big-M terms and adds penalty $\beta C_u$.
- **Objective:** trades off weighted delays, energy (favoring slower profiles), and cancellation costs.

The model is linear: all nonlinearities are avoided through the big-M disjunctive formulation and binary ordering variables.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $D \subset T \times T$ | ordered pairs of trains that may conflict (same direction) |
| $O \subset T \times T$ | pairs of trains running in **opposite directions** (bidirectional conflicts on shared track) |
| $\mathcal{B} \subset S$ | set of blocked segments during disruption window $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ |
| $P$ | set of cancellation decisions, $P \subseteq T$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r^{k}_{is}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $e^{k}_{is}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival, departure at stations, and segment separation |
| $d^{sch}_{is}, a^{sch}_{is}$ | scheduled departure/arrival of train $i$ at boundary of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority class) |
| $\alpha$ | monetary cost per unit of energy |
| $\beta_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $x^{ref}_{is}$ | =1 if rerouting to the opposite track is allowed for train $i$ on segment $s$ (only during $[t^{dis}_1,t^{dis}_2]$ and on blocked segments) |
| $H^{opp}$ | headway for opposite-direction trains sharing the same physical track |

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at the start of segment $s$

**Binary:**
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $s$
- $u_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ (written $u_{is,k}$)
- $\delta_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variable, =1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $\sigma_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ passes train $j$ (reordering) before segment $s$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \sum_{s \in S} \big[(a_{is} - a^{sch}_{is}) + (d_{is} - d^{sch}_{is})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k}}_{\text{energy cost}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} \beta_i y_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
\tag{1}
$$

(Delays can be linearized with $D_{is} \ge a_{is}-a^{sch}_{is}$, $D_{is}\ge 0$ if only positive delays are penalized.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness — exactly one profile per train-segment:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} u_{is,k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency (retiming via profile choice):**
$$
d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} r^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k} \le a_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{3}
$$

**(C3) Train chain continuity (no overtaking within a train's own path):**
$$
a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{4}
$$

**(C4) Dwell time at stations:**
$$
a_{i,s} + \tau^{min}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i,\ s \text{ at station boundaries} \tag{5}
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, with reordering):**
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge h^{seg} - M(1-\delta_{ij,s}) - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge h^{seg} - M\,\delta_{ij,s} - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6b}
$$

Analogous pairs with $d_{is}$ using $h^{dep}$ and with $a_{is}$ vs $d_{js}$ using $h^{arr}$.

**(C6) Rerouting to opposite track (only during disruption, only on blocked segments):**
$$
z_{is} \le x^{ref}_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{7}
$$
$$
z_{is} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ s \notin \mathcal{B} \tag{8}
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track:** if train $i$ (direction A) is rerouted onto the opposite track, it must not conflict with train $j$ (direction B) using its own track:
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - \delta_{ij,s}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - (1-\delta_{ij,s})) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9b}
$$

**(C8) Blocked segment closure during disruption window:** trains may traverse blocked segment $s \in \mathcal{B}$ only if rerouted ($z_{is}=1$) or outside the window:
$$
a_{is} \le t^{dis}_1 + M(1 - \lambda_{is}) \quad\text{or}\quad a_{is} \ge t^{dis}_2 - M \lambda_{is},\quad \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\lambda_{is} \le z_{is} + (1 - \text{window overlap indicator}) \quad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{10}
$$

**(C9) Reordering (overtaking) consistency across consecutive segments:**
$$
\delta_{ij,s} - \delta_{ij,s+1} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j, \qquad
\delta_{ij,s+1} - \delta_{ij,s} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j \tag{11}
$$
(overtaking allowed only if the passing variable $\sigma$ is activated, which in practice requires station tracks).

**(C10) Cancellation propagation:** a cancelled train occupies no resources:
$$
d_{is},\ a_{is} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i,\ s \tag{12}
$$

**(C11) Schedule adherence bounds / recovery limits:**
$$
a_{is} \le a^{sch}_{is} + \Delta^{max}_i \quad \forall i, s \tag{13}
$$

**(C12) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0; \quad y_i, z_{is}, u_{is,k}, \delta_{ij,s}, \sigma_{ij,s}, \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\} \tag{14}
$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling:** continuous $a_{is}, d_{is}$ allow retiming; binaries $\delta_{ij,s}$ allow resequencing (6), and $\sigma_{ij,s}$ permits overtaking at stations (11).
- **Rerouting:** $z_{is}$ sends a train onto the opposite track during the partial blockage (7)–(8); constraints (9) prevent head-on conflicts on the shared physical track.
- **Speed management:** discrete profiles $u_{is,k}$ couple running time (3) and energy (objective) — slower profiles save energy but may increase delays, capturing the delay–energy trade-off.
- **Cancellation:** $y_i$ removes a train entirely at penalty $\beta_i$ (2, 12).
- **Disruption handling:** (10) forbids occupancy of blocked segments during $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ unless rerouted.
- **Objective (1)** balances weighted delays, energy cost, and cancellation penalties, yielding a linear MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut.

Introduction

High-speed railways offer a rapid, efficient, and eco-friendly mode of transport that significantly enhances passenger mobility and drives regional economic growth. In recent years, the high-speed railway network has been undergoing continuing global expansion, resulting in increased traffic (Dal Sasso et al. 2022). In high-speed railway operations, train scheduling, as one of the most critical and challenging tasks, aims to execute and maintain a conflict-free timetable (Schälicke and Nachtigall 2025). However, the high-speed railway transport system is inherently complex and frequently subject to the impacts of unforeseen events, rendering the established timetable inexecutable. Based on severity, sudden events can be categorized into two types: disturbances and disruptions (Cacchiani et al. 2014). Disturbances are minor operational interruptions, such as slight delays during boarding, which can generally be managed within the existing timetable due to its inherent robustness. The core issue arising from minor disturbances is railway delay management (Flamini and Pacciarelli 2008; Schachtebeck and Schöbel 2010; Pellegrini, Marlière, and Rodriguez 2014). In contrast, disruptions are major operational interruptions causing substantial timetable modifications, that can severely affect train operations, leading to delays and increased operational costs (Kroon, Maróti, and Nielsen 2015; Borraz-Sánchez, Klabjan, and Uygur 2020; Croella et al. 2022). When a disruption occurs, some trains cannot travel normally in affected segments, leading to deviations from the scheduled times and rendering predesigned speed profiles inapplicable (Bärmann, Martin, and Schneider 2021). These events necessitate a systematic adjustment of operational strategies, including arrival and departure times adjustments (retiming), train order modifications (reordering), train reoute alterations (rerouting), or even train service cancellations, referred to as the train rescheduling problem (TRP) (D’Ariano et al. 2008; Veelenturf et al. 2016). Among disruptions, those caused by partial segment blockages occur commonly (Louwerse and Huisman 2014; Zhan et al. 2016). Such disruptions are often caused by factors such as equipment failures that prevent the normal passage of one side of the track. Trains are unable to pass through specific segments (i.e., disruption areas) at specific periods (i.e., during the disruption time window). Under such disruption scenarios, the TRP can incorporate local rerouting strategies. The rerouting strategy is designed to enhance operational flexibility and maintain unidirectional line capacity, allowing affected trains to divert to the opposite track within the disruption time window, thereby effectively mitigating delays. However, this strategy increases the complexity of the problem, as it introduces potential conflicts between bidirectional trains sharing the track resources, requiring the rescheduled timetable to precisely coordinate the paths and timing of bidirectional trains.

The implementation of a feasible rescheduling timetable of the TRP depends on the driving strategies at the train control level. Speed management translates operational-level dispatch instructions into precise and feasible train driving strategies, generating corresponding speed profiles to form the train speed management problem (TSMP) (Howlett, Pudney, and Albrecht 2022). The feasibility of a rescheduled timetable is directly contingent upon the feasibility of its corresponding speed profiles. This critical dependency highlights the necessity of incorporating speed management into disruption recovery frameworks. In partial segment blockage scenarios, trains must execute driving strategies based on optimized speed profiles of the TSMP, accelerating or decelerating in real time to meet the strict arrival/departure and inter-station running times requirements of the updated timetable, while passing through conflict zones. In this process, different speed profiles give rise to significant differences in energy consumption, thereby naturally establishing energy efficiency as an important co-optimization objective. Specifically, a disruption-affected train may either accelerate to arrive at the station earlier, which could necessitate an extended dwell time due to resource conflicts, or decelerate to align its arrival with the post-disruption recovery time, where these two strategies entail significantly distinct energy consumption patterns (Zhan et al. 2022).

The TRP and TSMP are closely related as inherent interdependencies exist between traffic-related properties (e.g., train running times, arrival and departure times) and train dynamics properties (e.g., train deceleration and acceleration) (Dong et al. 2021). Addressing these two problems separately fails to capture their intrinsic connection, may lead to rescheduling timetables that are infeasible at the control level, or to speed profiles that violate operational constraints, resulting in ineffective response to events (Yang et al. 2016). Consequently, the integrated optimization of train timetables and speed profiles under disruptions has emerged as a highly complex and challenging problem, referred to as the train rescheduling and speed management problem (TRSMP), attracting growing attention in high-speed railway operations research in recent years (e.g. Xu et al. 2017; Zhou et al. 2017; Xiu et al. 2025). In the context of partial blockages, the implementation of rerouting strategies further intensifies this complexity by amplifying potential conflicts between bidirectional trains, rendering the integrated problem a critical and yet unresolved challenge in the literature. Key challenges lie in synergistically resolving bidirectional train conflicts and the coupling between train rescheduling and speed management while rigorously ensuring the conflict-free operation of trains. This study proposes a novel integrated modeling and solution framework to address the TRSMP problem in a disruption caused by partial segment blockages, aiming to support coordinated rescheduling and control while facilitating rapid service recovery. Our scientific contribution is fivefold:

We introduce an innovative approach by integrating TRP and TSMP into a single framework, making this study one of the first to tackle both aspects simultaneously in the context of disruptions caused by partial segment blockages. This framework explicitly handles the dual challenges of bidirectional train conflict resolution on a shared track and the coupled decision-making between train rescheduling and speed control. It simultaneously optimizes the train times, orders, routes and speed profiles.

We propose a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that yields a conflict-free timetable and the corresponding executable speed profiles. Our formulation aligns train position and timing within the timetable with speed profiles, enhancing the accuracy and utility of the integrated model.

To tackle the computational complexity of the integrated model, we propose a decomposition-based solution method. We decompose the MILP into a reformulated integer programming (IP) model, focusing on train interactions, and a series of train plans, each addressing the operation of a single train. The integrated problem is transformed into a train plan selection problem. We have proved that the IP model with sufficiently fine interval plans is equivalent to the MILP.

We designed an adaptive iterative algorithm to address the combinatorial explosion of train plans and the potential infeasibility issues in the IP model. This algorithm iteratively refines the plan granularity within the neighborhood of the previous solution, thereby enhancing solution quality while maintaining computational efficiency. To further accelerate the process, we incorporate two tailored techniques with an adaptive refinement process and a local branching strategy.

Through extensive numerical experiments based on real-world scenarios, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the adaptive algorithm accelerates the solution process for large-scale instances compared to solving the MILP or the IP models.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: Section 2 reviews related literature on train rescheduling and integrated studies. Section 3 details the problem statement and assumptions. Section 4 outlines the MILP model formulation. Section 5 describes the solution framework. Section 6 presents case studies to demonstrate the practical application. Section 7 concludes the paper.

| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$ | disruption time window on blocked segment $s^* \in S$ (partial blockage: only one track usable) |
| $P_i \subseteq S$ | ordered sequence of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,s}^{k}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}^{k}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, segment separation (same direction) |
| $h^{bi}$ | minimum headway between opposing trains on the shared (opposite-direction) track during disruption |
| $d_i^{sch}, a_i^{sch}$ | scheduled departure/arrival times at origin/destination |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation in the objective |
| $C_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $H^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround/dwell time at stations |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t^{res}$ | time at which the disrupted track is restored |

## 3. Variables

**Rescheduling:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at the boundary of segment $s$ (station node).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$.
- $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ run in **opposite directions** and $i$ uses the shared track before $j$.
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies the shared opposite track on segment $s$ during the disruption (rerouting).

**Speed selection:**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \big[(a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}) + (d_{i,1} - d_i^{sch})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in P_i}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

(Delay terms can be linearized with $\ge 0$ auxiliary variables $D_i \ge a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}$, $D_i \ge 0$.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_i} \delta_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (retiming via speed choice):**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s'} = \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k} \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i,\; s' = \text{downstream node of } s$$

**(C3) Minimum dwell/turnaround at stations:**
$$a_{i,s} + H^{turn} \le d_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; \forall \text{ station nodes } s$$

**(C4) Cancellation forbids movement:**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i), \qquad a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, allows reordering):**
$$a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{seg} - M(1 - x_{ij}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$
$$a_{i,s} - a_{j,s} \ge h^{seg} - M\,x_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$

**(C6) Station headways (arrival/departure):**
$$d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1-x_{ij}), \qquad a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{arr} - M(1-x_{ij})$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M x_{ij}$, for all $(i,j)\in O$, stations $s$.

**(C7) Rerouting to the shared opposite track during disruption:**
$$u_{i,s^*} \le y^{win}_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i$$
where $y^{win}_{i,s^*}$ (linearized) enforces that train $i$ may use the shared track only if its occupancy window intersects $\mathcal{D}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \le t_d^{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s^*}), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s^*})$$
i.e., $u_{i,s^*}=1$ only if the train is on $s^*$ within the disruption window; otherwise it must wait for $t^{res}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^{res} - M\,u_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i \text{ (single-track direction)}$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track:** for opposing trains $i,j$ both potentially on $s^*$ during $\mathcal{D}$:
$$d_{i,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
so if both use the shared track, exactly one order ($z_{ij}$ or $1-z_{ij}$) is enforced.

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-cycle / transitivity on triplets):**
$$x_{ij} + x_{jk} - x_{ik} \le 1, \quad x_{ij} + x_{jk} \ge x_{ik} \quad \forall i,j,k \in T$$

**(C10) Time bounds:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling variables** ($a, d, x, y$) allow retiming (C2 with chosen running times), reordering (C5–C6, C9), and cancellation (C4, C10).
- **Rerouting** is captured by $u_{i,s^*}$: during the disruption window trains may be routed onto the opposite track (C7); otherwise they must wait until restoration.
- **Speed management** is modeled by discrete profiles $\delta_{i,s}^k$ with fixed $(r^k, e^k)$ pairs, coupling timetable decisions and energy (C1–C2). Slower profiles reduce energy but may increase delays — the objective trades these off.
- **Safety** is ensured by headway constraints on segments and stations (C5–C6) and by the big-M bidirectional conflict constraints (C8) preventing simultaneous opposing occupancy of the shared track.
- **Objective** minimizes weighted total delay, total traction energy, and cancellation penalties, with weights $\alpha, \beta$ tuning the trade-off.

All constraints are linear; binary variables are $y_i, x_{ij}, z_{ij}, u_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}^k$, so the model is a valid MILP.

Model 2:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $P$ | set of platform tracks at each station, indexed $p$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^-, t_d^+]$ | disruption time window during which one track of a blocked segment $s^* \in S$ is unavailable |
| $U$ | set of trains eligible for cancellation, indexed $u$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $h^{seg}, h^{arr}, h^{dep}$ | minimum headways: same-direction segment, arrival, departure |
| $\tau_i^{run}(s,k)$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_i(s,k)$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $\tau_i^{dwell}(s)$ | planned dwell time of train $i$ at station bounding segment $s$ |
| $t_i^{sched}(s)$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority) |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation penalty |
| $C_u$ | cancellation penalty of train $u$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $\bar{t}$ | planning horizon end |
| $o_i \in \{0,1\}$ | parameter: 1 if train $i$ is scheduled on the track opposite to the blocked one (direction indicator) |

## 3. Variables

**Timing variables**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ from the start of segment $s$
- $\delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0$: arrival / departure delay

**Speed profile selection**
- $x_{isk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$

**Routing / reordering / rerouting**
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ (ordering variable, $i<j$)
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite (shared) track on segment $s$ during the disruption
- $q_{isp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies platform track $p$ at station $s$

**Cancellation**
- $c_u \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $u$ is cancelled

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \big(w_i \delta_{is}^{arr} + w_i \delta_{is}^{dep}\big)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_i(s,k)\, x_{isk}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{u \in U} C_u c_u}_{\text{cancellation penalties}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{is}^{arr} \ge a_{is} - t_i^{sched}(s), \quad \delta_{is}^{arr} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (speed profile coupling)**
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} \tau_i^{run}(s,k)\, x_{isk} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Dwell time**
$$
d_{i,s+1} \ge a_{is} + \tau_i^{dwell}(s+1) \qquad \forall i,\; s = 1,\dots,|S|-1
$$

**(C4) Speed profile uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in U,\; \forall s; \qquad \sum_{k \in K_i} x_{isk} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \setminus U,\; \forall s
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segments (with reordering)**
For all pairs $i < j$ on the same track and direction:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{seg} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M c_j
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js} + h^{seg} - M\, y_{ij} - M c_i
$$

**(C6) Rerouting to the opposite track during disruption**
For segment $s^*$ and $t \in \mathcal{D}$: a train may use the blocked track only if it does not traverse during $\mathcal{D}$, or it is rerouted:
$$
a_{is^*} \ge t_d^+ - M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) - M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \le t_d^- + M\big(1 - z_{is^*}\big) + M c_i \qquad \forall i
$$
i.e., if $z_{is^*}=0$ and the train is not cancelled, it must completely avoid $\mathcal{D}$ on the blocked track; $z_{is^*}=1$ forces rerouting to the shared opposite track.

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track**
Trains rerouted onto the shared track ($z=1$) and trains normally operating in the opposite direction ($o_j = 1$) must not occupy segment $s^*$ simultaneously. For all pairs $i,j$ with $o_j = 1$:
$$
d_{js^*} \ge a_{is^*} + h^{seg} - M(3 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) - y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
$$
d_{is^*} \ge a_{js^*} + h^{seg} - M(2 - z_{is^*} - (1-o_j) + y_{ij}) - M(c_i + c_j)
$$
The big-M structure ensures these constraints are active only when train $i$ is rerouted onto the shared track and train $j$ runs in the opposite direction, with the ordering variable $y_{ij}$ selecting which train goes first.

**(C8) Station headways (arrival/departure)**
For trains assigned to the same platform track $p$ at station $s$:
$$
a_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{arr} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
$$
d_{js} \ge d_{is} + h^{dep} - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - q_{isp} - q_{jsp}) - M(c_i+c_j)
$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M y_{ij}$.

**(C9) Platform track assignment uniqueness**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} q_{isp} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s \text{ (station nodes)}
$$

**(C10) Horizon bounds**
$$
a_{is} \le \bar{t}, \quad d_{is} \le \bar{t} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C11) Variable domains**
$$
x_{isk}, y_{ij}, z_{is}, q_{isp}, c_u \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is}^{arr}, \delta_{is}^{dep} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Model Explanation

- **Rescheduling:** Constraints (C1)–(C3) allow retiming (shifted arrival/departure) and enforce physical running and dwell times; reordering is enabled by the binary $y_{ij}$ in (C5), (C7), (C8).
- **Speed management:** Each train–segment picks exactly one discrete profile (C4); each profile has a fixed running time and energy, coupling the timing and energy dimensions of the objective.
- **Disruption handling:** (C6) forces trains either to wait until the disruption ends or to be rerouted to the opposite track; (C7) guarantees conflict-free bidirectional operation on the shared track.
- **Cancellations:** $c_u$ deactivates all constraints of a cancelled train via big-M terms and adds penalty $\beta C_u$.
- **Objective:** trades off weighted delays, energy (favoring slower profiles), and cancellation costs.

The model is linear: all nonlinearities are avoided through the big-M disjunctive formulation and binary ordering variables.

Model 3:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $D \subset T \times T$ | ordered pairs of trains that may conflict (same direction) |
| $O \subset T \times T$ | pairs of trains running in **opposite directions** (bidirectional conflicts on shared track) |
| $\mathcal{B} \subset S$ | set of blocked segments during disruption window $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ |
| $P$ | set of cancellation decisions, $P \subseteq T$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r^{k}_{is}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $e^{k}_{is}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival, departure at stations, and segment separation |
| $d^{sch}_{is}, a^{sch}_{is}$ | scheduled departure/arrival of train $i$ at boundary of segment $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority class) |
| $\alpha$ | monetary cost per unit of energy |
| $\beta_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $x^{ref}_{is}$ | =1 if rerouting to the opposite track is allowed for train $i$ on segment $s$ (only during $[t^{dis}_1,t^{dis}_2]$ and on blocked segments) |
| $H^{opp}$ | headway for opposite-direction trains sharing the same physical track |

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at the start of segment $s$

**Binary:**
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $s$
- $u_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ (written $u_{is,k}$)
- $\delta_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variable, =1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $\sigma_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: =1 if train $i$ passes train $j$ (reordering) before segment $s$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \sum_{s \in S} \big[(a_{is} - a^{sch}_{is}) + (d_{is} - d^{sch}_{is})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k}}_{\text{energy cost}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} \beta_i y_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
\tag{1}
$$

(Delays can be linearized with $D_{is} \ge a_{is}-a^{sch}_{is}$, $D_{is}\ge 0$ if only positive delays are penalized.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness — exactly one profile per train-segment:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_i} u_{is,k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency (retiming via profile choice):**
$$
d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_i} r^{k}_{is}\, u_{is,k} \le a_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{3}
$$

**(C3) Train chain continuity (no overtaking within a train's own path):**
$$
a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{4}
$$

**(C4) Dwell time at stations:**
$$
a_{i,s} + \tau^{min}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s+1} \quad \forall i,\ s \text{ at station boundaries} \tag{5}
$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, with reordering):**
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge h^{seg} - M(1-\delta_{ij,s}) - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge h^{seg} - M\,\delta_{ij,s} - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in D \tag{6b}
$$

Analogous pairs with $d_{is}$ using $h^{dep}$ and with $a_{is}$ vs $d_{js}$ using $h^{arr}$.

**(C6) Rerouting to opposite track (only during disruption, only on blocked segments):**
$$
z_{is} \le x^{ref}_{is} \quad \forall i \in T,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{7}
$$
$$
z_{is} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ s \notin \mathcal{B} \tag{8}
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track:** if train $i$ (direction A) is rerouted onto the opposite track, it must not conflict with train $j$ (direction B) using its own track:
$$
a_{js} - a_{is} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - \delta_{ij,s}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9a}
$$
$$
a_{is} - a_{js} \ge H^{opp} - M(3 - z_{is} - (1-z_{js}) - (1-\delta_{ij,s})) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9b}
$$

**(C8) Blocked segment closure during disruption window:** trains may traverse blocked segment $s \in \mathcal{B}$ only if rerouted ($z_{is}=1$) or outside the window:
$$
a_{is} \le t^{dis}_1 + M(1 - \lambda_{is}) \quad\text{or}\quad a_{is} \ge t^{dis}_2 - M \lambda_{is},\quad \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\lambda_{is} \le z_{is} + (1 - \text{window overlap indicator}) \quad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{B} \tag{10}
$$

**(C9) Reordering (overtaking) consistency across consecutive segments:**
$$
\delta_{ij,s} - \delta_{ij,s+1} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j, \qquad
\delta_{ij,s+1} - \delta_{ij,s} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + y_i + y_j \tag{11}
$$
(overtaking allowed only if the passing variable $\sigma$ is activated, which in practice requires station tracks).

**(C10) Cancellation propagation:** a cancelled train occupies no resources:
$$
d_{is},\ a_{is} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i,\ s \tag{12}
$$

**(C11) Schedule adherence bounds / recovery limits:**
$$
a_{is} \le a^{sch}_{is} + \Delta^{max}_i \quad \forall i, s \tag{13}
$$

**(C12) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0; \quad y_i, z_{is}, u_{is,k}, \delta_{ij,s}, \sigma_{ij,s}, \lambda_{is} \in \{0,1\} \tag{14}
$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling:** continuous $a_{is}, d_{is}$ allow retiming; binaries $\delta_{ij,s}$ allow resequencing (6), and $\sigma_{ij,s}$ permits overtaking at stations (11).
- **Rerouting:** $z_{is}$ sends a train onto the opposite track during the partial blockage (7)–(8); constraints (9) prevent head-on conflicts on the shared physical track.
- **Speed management:** discrete profiles $u_{is,k}$ couple running time (3) and energy (objective) — slower profiles save energy but may increase delays, capturing the delay–energy trade-off.
- **Cancellation:** $y_i$ removes a train entirely at penalty $\beta_i$ (2, 12).
- **Disruption handling:** (10) forbids occupancy of blocked segments during $[t^{dis}_1, t^{dis}_2]$ unless rerouted.
- **Objective (1)** balances weighted delays, energy cost, and cancellation penalties, yielding a linear MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut.

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,s}^{k}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}^{k}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, segment separation (same direction) |
| $h^{bi}$ | minimum headway between opposing trains on the shared (opposite-direction) track during disruption |
| $d_i^{sch}, a_i^{sch}$ | scheduled departure/arrival times at origin/destination |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation in the objective |
| $C_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $H^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround/dwell time at stations |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t^{res}$ | time at which the disrupted track is restored |

## 3. Variables

**Rescheduling:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at the boundary of segment $s$ (station node).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$.
- $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ run in **opposite directions** and $i$ uses the shared track before $j$.
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies the shared opposite track on segment $s$ during the disruption (rerouting).

**Speed selection:**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \big[(a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}) + (d_{i,1} - d_i^{sch})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in P_i}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

(Delay terms can be linearized with $\ge 0$ auxiliary variables $D_i \ge a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}$, $D_i \ge 0$.)

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_i} \delta_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (retiming via speed choice):**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s'} = \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k} \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i,\; s' = \text{downstream node of } s$$

**(C3) Minimum dwell/turnaround at stations:**
$$a_{i,s} + H^{turn} \le d_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; \forall \text{ station nodes } s$$

**(C4) Cancellation forbids movement:**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i), \qquad a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, allows reordering):**
$$a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{seg} - M(1 - x_{ij}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$
$$a_{i,s} - a_{j,s} \ge h^{seg} - M\,x_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$

**(C6) Station headways (arrival/departure):**
$$d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1-x_{ij}), \qquad a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{arr} - M(1-x_{ij})$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M x_{ij}$, for all $(i,j)\in O$, stations $s$.

**(C7) Rerouting to the shared opposite track during disruption:**
$$u_{i,s^*} \le y^{win}_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i$$
where $y^{win}_{i,s^*}$ (linearized) enforces that train $i$ may use the shared track only if its occupancy window intersects $\mathcal{D}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \le t_d^{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s^*}), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s^*})$$
i.e., $u_{i,s^*}=1$ only if the train is on $s^*$ within the disruption window; otherwise it must wait for $t^{res}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^{res} - M\,u_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i \text{ (single-track direction)}$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track:** for opposing trains $i,j$ both potentially on $s^*$ during $\mathcal{D}$:
$$d_{i,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
so if both use the shared track, exactly one order ($z_{ij}$ or $1-z_{ij}$) is enforced.

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-cycle / transitivity on triplets):**
$$x_{ij} + x_{jk} - x_{ik} \le 1, \quad x_{ij} + x_{jk} \ge x_{ik} \quad \forall i,j,k \in T$$

**(C10) Time bounds:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling variables** ($a, d, x, y$) allow retiming (C2 with chosen running times), reordering (C5–C6, C9), and cancellation (C4, C10).
- **Rerouting** is captured by $u_{i,s^*}$: during the disruption window trains may be routed onto the opposite track (C7); otherwise they must wait until restoration.
- **Speed management** is modeled by discrete profiles $\delta_{i,s}^k$ with fixed $(r^k, e^k)$ pairs, coupling timetable decisions and energy (C1–C2). Slower profiles reduce energy but may increase delays — the objective trades these off.
- **Safety** is ensured by headway constraints on segments and stations (C5–C6) and by the big-M bidirectional conflict constraints (C8) preventing simultaneous opposing occupancy of the shared track.
- **Objective** minimizes weighted total delay, total traction energy, and cancellation penalties, with weights $\alpha, \beta$ tuning the trade-off.

All constraints are linear; binary variables are $y_i, x_{ij}, z_{ij}, u_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}^k$, so the model is a valid MILP.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (blocks) on the line, indexed $s$; stations are boundaries between segments |
| $K_i$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on each segment, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = [t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$ | disruption time window on blocked segment $s^* \in S$ (partial blockage: only one track usable) |
| $P_i \subseteq S$ | ordered sequence of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,s}^{k}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}^{k}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, segment separation (same direction) |
| $h^{bi}$ | minimum headway between opposing trains on the shared (opposite-direction) track during disruption |
| $d_i^{sch}, a_i^{sch}$ | scheduled departure/arrival times at origin/destination |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for energy and cancellation in the objective |
| $C_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $H^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround/dwell time at stations |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t^{res}$ | time at which the disrupted track is restored |

## 3. Variables

**Rescheduling:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at the boundary of segment $s$ (station node).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$.
- $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ run in **opposite directions** and $i$ uses the shared track before $j$.
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies the shared opposite track on segment $s$ during the disruption (rerouting).

**Speed selection:**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w_i \big[(a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}) + (d_{i,1} - d_i^{sch})\big]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in P_i}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

(Delay terms can be linearized with $\ge 0$ auxiliary variables $D_i \ge a_{i,|P_i|} - a_i^{sch}$, $D_i \ge 0$.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_i} \delta_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (retiming via speed choice):**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s'} = \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s}^{k}\,\delta_{i,s}^{k} \quad \forall i,\; \forall s \in P_i,\; s' = \text{downstream node of } s$$

**(C3) Minimum dwell/turnaround at stations:**
$$a_{i,s} + H^{turn} \le d_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; \forall \text{ station nodes } s$$

**(C4) Cancellation forbids movement:**
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i), \qquad a_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Same-direction headway on segment $s$ (conflict-free, allows reordering):**
$$a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{seg} - M(1 - x_{ij}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$
$$a_{i,s} - a_{j,s} \ge h^{seg} - M\,x_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\; \forall s$$

**(C6) Station headways (arrival/departure):**
$$d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1-x_{ij}), \qquad a_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h^{arr} - M(1-x_{ij})$$
and symmetric counterparts with $M x_{ij}$, for all $(i,j)\in O$, stations $s$.

**(C7) Rerouting to the shared opposite track during disruption:**
$$u_{i,s^*} \le y^{win}_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i$$
where $y^{win}_{i,s^*}$ (linearized) enforces that train $i$ may use the shared track only if its occupancy window intersects $\mathcal{D}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \le t_d^{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s^*}), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s^*})$$
i.e., $u_{i,s^*}=1$ only if the train is on $s^*$ within the disruption window; otherwise it must wait for $t^{res}$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^{res} - M\,u_{i,s^*} \quad \forall i \text{ (single-track direction)}$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track:** for opposing trains $i,j$ both potentially on $s^*$ during $\mathcal{D}$:
$$d_{i,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h^{bi} \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - u_{i,s^*} - u_{j,s^*} - z_{ij})$$
so if both use the shared track, exactly one order ($z_{ij}$ or $1-z_{ij}$) is enforced.

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-cycle / transitivity on triplets):**
$$x_{ij} + x_{jk} - x_{ik} \le 1, \quad x_{ij} + x_{jk} \ge x_{ik} \quad \forall i,j,k \in T$$

**(C10) Time bounds:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Rescheduling variables** ($a, d, x, y$) allow retiming (C2 with chosen running times), reordering (C5–C6, C9), and cancellation (C4, C10).
- **Rerouting** is captured by $u_{i,s^*}$: during the disruption window trains may be routed onto the opposite track (C7); otherwise they must wait until restoration.
- **Speed management** is modeled by discrete profiles $\delta_{i,s}^k$ with fixed $(r^k, e^k)$ pairs, coupling timetable decisions and energy (C1–C2). Slower profiles reduce energy but may increase delays — the objective trades these off.
- **Safety** is ensured by headway constraints on segments and stations (C5–C6) and by the big-M bidirectional conflict constraints (C8) preventing simultaneous opposing occupancy of the shared track.
- **Objective** minimizes weighted total delay, total traction energy, and cancellation penalties, with weights $\alpha, \beta$ tuning the trade-off.

All constraints are linear; binary variables are $y_i, x_{ij}, z_{ij}, u_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}^k$, so the model is a valid MILP.
